paragraphs: Friend, this one is heavy, and I think it hurts. Before the fight, Jephthah vows to the LORD that "whatever comes out the door of my house to greet me…" will belong to the LORD (Judges 11:31). Then his daughter walks out with tambourines and dancing (Judges 11:34), and he says, "I have given my word to the LORD and cannot take it back" (Judges 11:35). Those words show how heavy a promise to the LORD was to him.

Here's what I take from it, baker. Words said to the LORD carry weight, so slow down before you make a promise. A vow made in a big, loud moment can still be there in a quiet one. Before you say "I'll do anything," stop and ask what "anything" could cost you.

I also want you to see his daughter. She answers, "My father, you have given your word to the LORD" (Judges 11:36), and she asks for two months in the mountains with her friends (Judges 11:37). Each year the young women of Israel go out for four days to lament her (Judges 11:40), so the Bible keeps her remembered. And friend, Jephthah's story isn't over yet.
